extracted.intended_audience: pipeline operators, pipeline integrity/safety engineers, and company compliance officers
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and evaluation criteria for installing, operating, maintaining, and documenting remote/automatic/manual valves (RMVs) and alternative equivalent technologies on onshore gas, hazardous liquid, and carbon dioxide pipelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and approval for alternative equivalent technology
rubrics_metrics.description: If an operator seeks to install alternative equivalent technology, the operator must, in advance of such installation, submit a notification making such a request to PHMSA in accordance with § 192.18 (or § 195.18). The operator must include in that notification a site-specific technical and safety evaluation demonstrating that technology provides an equivalent level of safety to an RMV.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site-specific evaluation should reference factors including, but not limited to: design, construction, maintenance, and operating procedures; technology design and operational characteristics such as operation times (closure times for manual valves); service reliability and life; accessibility to operator personnel; nearby population density; and potential consequences to the environment and the public. PHMSA retains discretion to reject requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstration required when proposing manual valves as alternative
rubrics_metrics.description: If an operator requests use of manual valves as an alternative equivalent technology, the notification submitted to PHMSA must also demonstrate the site-specific economic, technical, or operational infeasibility of installing an RMV.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of supporting factors: access to communications and power; terrain; prohibitive cost; labor and component availability; ability to secure required land access rights and permits; and accessibility to operator personnel for installation and maintenance. Operators in non-HCAs may request exemptions from certain operation requirements but must provide closing times for those manual valves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for extension of compliance deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: An operator may submit a project-specific request for extension of the compliance deadline demonstrating that installation of an RMV or alternative equivalent technology in connection with near-term construction and replacement projects would be economically, technically, or operationally infeasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notifications for extensions must reference factors such as prohibitive economic costs, difficulty securing access rights, component/labor availability and procurement lead times, and permitting requirements. PHMSA reviews such requests under the notification procedures (§ 192.18/§ 195.18).

rubrics_metrics.name: Valve spacing requirements (general and by program)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule prescribes maximum distances between RMVs or alternative equivalent technologies depending on pipeline type, class location, and whether the line could affect HCAs or is an HVL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from the rule include: for certain replaced gas segments: not to exceed 4 miles (Class 4), 7.5 miles (Class 3), and 10 miles (other locations) in one context; §192.634 spacing: not exceed 8 miles (Class 4), 15 miles (Class 3), and 20 miles (other locations); hazardous liquid §195.260 spacing: pipelines that could affect HCAs — not exceed 15 miles; pipelines that could not affect HCAs — not exceed 20 miles. HVL pipelines in high-population/other populated areas: maximum spacing 7.5 miles (with possible increase by 1.25x to a maximum of 9 3/8 miles subject to PHMSA review and demonstration of infeasibility). Maximum spacing between valves protecting multiple adjacent water crossings cannot exceed 1 mile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change in Class Location: valve installation and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: When a class location changes, operators must install valves (including RMVs or alternative equivalent technology) as necessary to comply, and must install such valves within 24 months of the class location change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an operator replaces less than 2 miles of pipe in a length of 5 contiguous miles of pipe during a 24-month period to comply with MOP requirements after a class location change, the operator must either comply with valve spacing requirements at § 192.179(a) or install/use RMVs so that the entirety of the replaced segment is between 2 RMVs and so that the distance between those valves does not exceed 20 miles. Operators need not comply with section if they replace less than 1,000 feet within any single contiguous mile within any 24-month period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency procedures must provide for rupture mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Emergency procedures in operators' procedural manuals must provide for rupture mitigation in response to a rupture event and require liaison with appropriate public safety answering points (e.g., 9-1-1) if available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators may establish liaison with local emergency coordinating agencies (9-1-1 centers, county emergency managers) instead of communicating with individual fire/police entities. Operators must learn responsibilities, resources, jurisdictional areas, and emergency contact telephone numbers for each federal, state, and local organization that may respond and inform such officials of the operator's ability to respond and communicate during pipeline emergencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of potential rupture: identification procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators must have written procedures that, upon notification of a potential rupture, identify whether there is indeed a rupture by specifying the sources of information, operational factors, and other criteria used to evaluate a notification as an actual rupture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written procedures should incorporate waiver procedures to waive on‑scene investigations for specific personnel if operator receives: multiple or recurring instrument indications (pressure readings, alarms), pressure drops significantly in excess of minimum thresholds (§ 192.635(a)(1) / § 195.417(a)(1)), or reports of rupture indicia from credible on‑scene sources (operator personnel, law enforcement, fire department, other emergency responders).

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-incident/failure analysis and lessons learned
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators must conduct post-event analyses of ruptures and other failure events involving activation of RMVs or alternative equivalent technologies, identify potential preventive and mitigative measures, and implement lessons learned throughout procedures and programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-incident review should include detection and mitigation actions, response time, valve location, valve actuation, and SCADA performance. Operators must complete a summary within 90 days, perform quarterly status reviews until final summary is prepared, have final summary and all associated reviews/analyses reviewed, dated, and signed by an appropriate senior executive officer, and retain final summary, investigation documents, and lessons-learned records for the useful life of the pipeline. (Some provisions exempt gas distribution and certain gathering pipelines.)

rubrics_metrics.name: RMV and alternative technology operational requirements (closing time)
rubrics_metrics.description: Following identification of a rupture, an operator must, after identifying a rupture, close RMVs or alternative equivalent technologies as soon as practicable, but no later than within 30 minutes (measured from rupture identification), unless a shorter shut-down time used in worst-case discharge calculations applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators may plan to leave RMVs open for longer than 30 minutes only if they have previously coordinated the plan with appropriate local emergency responders, notified PHMSA, and demonstrated that closing valves would be detrimental to public safety. For hazardous liquid pipelines, the shorter of 30 minutes or worst-case discharge shut-down time applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: RMV monitoring and operational capability
rubrics_metrics.description: RMVs and alternative equivalent technologies must be capable of being monitored or controlled by remote or on-site personnel, operated during all operating conditions, and monitored for valve status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators using ASVs as RMVs do not need to monitor those valves remotely if they have the capability to monitor pressures or gas/product flow rate on the pipeline to identify and locate a rupture pursuant to the rule. Operators in non-HCAs may request exemptions for manual valves' operation requirements but must provide closing times for those manual valves in notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valve maintenance, validation drills, and confirmation testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators must conduct maintenance, inspection, initial validation drills, and periodic confirmation drills to ensure valves (RMVs or alternative equivalent technologies) can close as soon as practicable but within the 30-minute requirement (or shorter worst-case discharge shut-down time).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drills need not fully close a valve; a closure of 25 percent, at minimum, is sufficient unless additional closure is required by operator information. If the 30-minute closure cannot be achieved during the drill, the operator must revise response efforts and repair valves to achieve compliance as soon as practicable but no later than 12 months after the drill; operators may request extension of the 12-month repair timeline for economic/technical/operational infeasibility. Alternative valve shut-off measures must be in place within 7 days of a failed drill. Operators must identify corrective actions and lessons learned and share/implement them across the network.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point-to-point verification for RCVs/controls and SCADA
rubrics_metrics.description: For each RCV installed under the rule, the operator must conduct a point-to-point verification between SCADA displays, installed valves, sensors, and communications equipment, or perform an equivalent verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referenced in §§ 192.631(c)/(e) and § 195.446(c)/(e). Ensures that remote control/indication paths are functionally verified end-to-end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shut-off segment definition and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'shut-off segment' is a pipeline segment entirely located between at least two RMVs or alternative equivalent technologies; if crossover or lateral pipes connect to the shut-off segment between upstream-most and downstream-most RMVs, the shut-off segment extends to valves on those connections so that, when all valves are closed, there is no flow path from outside the shut-off segment to the rupture site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Laterals contributing less than 5 percent of the total shut-off segment volume may have RMVs or alternative equivalent technologies installed at locations other than mainline receipt or delivery points. A shut-off segment can include multiple HCAs. Operators are not required to select the closest valve to the shut-off segment as an RMV as long as proper valve spacing is maintained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability thresholds for installations
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements to install RMVs or alternative equivalent technologies apply to newly constructed and entirely replaced onshore pipeline segments with diameters of 6 inches or greater (or ≥6 inches for hazardous liquid/CO2), and to 'entirely replaced' segments defined by replacement of 2 or more miles within any length of 5 contiguous miles during any 24-month period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some exclusions: the RMV/alternative requirements do not apply to certain pipe segments in Class 1 or Class 2 locations that have a PIR ≤ 150 feet; summary-report requirements are not applicable to gas distribution and certain gathering pipelines. The rule applies to segments constructed or meeting definition after April 10, 2023 (in hazardous liquid context).

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk analyses and senior executive certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk analyses and assessments conducted under the preventive-and-mitigative-measure provisions must be reviewed by the operator and certified by a senior executive of the company at least once per calendar year (period between reviews not to exceed 15 months) and also within 3 months of an incident or a safety-related condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses must consider new or existing operational and integrity matters that could affect rupture-mitigation processes and procedures. For certain onshore hazardous liquid pipelines, these risk analyses must be completed prior to placing into service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valve location for pipelines crossing wide waterways and floodplain requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For pipelines that cross waterways more than 100 feet wide (high water mark to high water mark), operators must install valves at locations outside of the 100-year flood plain or install valves equipped with control equipment that would not be made inoperable by flood conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also, maximum spacing between valves protecting multiple adjacent water crossings cannot exceed 1 mile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operator documentation, retention, and executive review
rubrics_metrics.description: Final post-incident summaries and all reviews/analyses required by these sections must be reviewed, dated, and signed by the operator's appropriate senior executive officer and retained for the useful life of the pipeline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators must also keep all investigation and analysis documents used to prepare the summary and records of lessons learned for the useful life of the pipeline. Quarterly status reviews are required while investigation is pending.

rubrics_metrics.name: HVL-specific spacing and alternate spacing approval process
rubrics_metrics.description: For HVL pipelines in high-population or other populated areas, maximum valve spacing is 7 1/2 miles if constructed or where 2 or more miles have been replaced within a span of 5 contiguous miles within 24 months; the spacing may be increased by 1.25 times (up to 9 3/8 miles) if the operator submits for PHMSA review an evaluation of the safety of the alternative spacing and a demonstration that installation at the otherwise-required spacing is economically, technically, or operationally infeasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The evaluation must reference technical and safety factors including design, construction, maintenance, operating procedures, potential consequences to the environment and public, and mitigation measures. Demonstration of infeasibility may reference access to communications/power, terrain, cost, labor/component availability, permitting, and land access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent notification procedure across parts and PHMSA discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators can notify PHMSA in advance of intent to use differing technology, compliance timeline, or method when specifically provided in regulatory text; PHMSA retains discretion under notification provisions to reject requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule revises parts 192 and 195 to provide consistent notification procedures (§ 192.18 and § 195.18) whenever an operator is required to notify PHMSA as part of the final rule. Notifications should be submitted in advance of installations, requests for exemptions, or requests for compliance deadline extensions.
